title: IBPS Clerk CSA: mains practice and local-language readiness
description: Build a CSA mains review cycle around data interpretation, reasoning, language and awareness, with official date context and local-language checks.
intro: IBPS’s official tentative calendar lists CSA-XVI mains on 27 December 2026. The prelims dates are already past, but no new prelims-result release was verified in this review. Prepare for the next stage while keeping a tentative schedule separate from a result or call-letter announcement.

sections.title: Use the current CSA structure
sections.body:
Check the CSA-XVI notification before reusing an old mains mock: section structure, timing and weighted marks can change between cycles. Keep a line for each section's attempts, accuracy and time pressure rather than comparing only the final total.

Make one diagnostic from a timed block. If you are choosing the wrong data set, practise selection; if your setup is wrong, repair the concept; if you simply calculate slowly, isolate the arithmetic. The [Clerk pattern page](/exams/ibps-clerk/exam-pattern/) summarises the cycle, while the notification controls the actual rules.

sections.title: Practise DI with a source-of-number check
sections.body:
For every calculation, point to the row, column and unit supplying the input. Distinguish total, average, percentage share and percentage change. Before using a shortcut, estimate whether the result should be above or below half the total.

Review [data interpretation](/quant/data-interpretation/) and [percentages](/quant/percentage/). Use a simple example: 120 out of 300 is a 40% share. If the value later becomes 150, the increase is 25% of 120, not 10% of 300. Write which question you are answering before doing either calculation.

sections.title: Use constraints in reasoning and context in English
sections.body:
In a puzzle, write fixed information first and mark assumptions as cases. Do not quietly turn “not next to” into “opposite”. When a branch leads to contradiction, record which condition caused it; this can expose a misread statement rather than a hard puzzle.

For English, choose an answer the sentence or passage supports. Keep a vocabulary record with context, not just translations. Review a short passage with the [evidence method](/study-guides/reading-comprehension-find-evidence/). Alternate focused repair with mixed sets so you practise recognising the question type under time pressure.

sections.title: Keep local-language and document conditions visible
sections.body:
Read the state/UT and local-language provisions in the current CSA notice, including what educational evidence is accepted and when a test may apply. Do not assume a good written score waives a language requirement.

Check your application state/UT and claimed-language evidence before later-stage instructions arrive. Review banking awareness from dated reliable sources, then explain each item in two sentences. The [CSA dates page](/exams/ibps-clerk/calendar/) uses 27 December as tentative; an actual mains call letter and any revised notice remain authoritative.

drills.prompt: 120 of 300 transactions use a channel. What is the share?
That channel grows from 120 to 150 transactions. What is its percentage increase?
drills.explanation: The increase is 30 and the original base is 120: 30/120 × 100 = 25. This is different from the channel’s share of all transactions.

checklist: Read the current CSA mains timing and marks.
Audit one DI set for units and bases.
Check state/UT language and document conditions.

faqs.q: Does the tentative mains date establish prelims qualification?
faqs.a: No. Qualification comes from the matching official prelims result.

faqs.q: Does a written score remove the local-language requirement?
faqs.a: Follow the current notice and accepted evidence or test provisions. Do not assume it is waived.
